subject.title: feat: add opt-in telemetry for native chat lifecycle

question: Should native chat lifecycle telemetry become a supported operator-facing contract with the full signal set proposed by this PR?
rationale: Correctness and proof are strong, but automation cannot decide whether the long-term diagnostic value justifies twenty new instruments and a second lifecycle state machine coupled to the chat provider.

options.title: Accept the bounded contract
options.body: Land the current signal set with its documented privacy, cardinality, opt-in, and lifecycle invariants as the supported initial contract.

options.title: Narrow the initial surface
options.body: Keep only the core turn, send, wait, and receive signals now, deferring history, drop, and secondary lifecycle instruments until operators demonstrate a need.

options.title: Defer native chat telemetry
options.body: Close or pause the PR until cross-process trace propagation or a broader observability design establishes a unified lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Land the current signal set with its documented privacy, cardinality, opt-in, and lifecycle invariants as the supported initial contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline provides the only explicit human routing signal connected to the current-head review after proof was accepted.
